review_method: Read JSON and historical contract/source text only; resolve source aliases and JSON property paths without importing owner modules or issuing live objects.

checks.name: family_prefixed_nonwrapping_sequence
checks.evidence: Eight distinct prefixes w,c,x,a,t,r,o,d with exact 16-digit lowercase hex suffix, positive 63-bit range and excluded zero have an injective 17-ASCII-byte representation. Prefix/domain validation and shared atomic reservation semantics prevent lexical class aliasing; original-object and HMAC checks remain the authentication barrier.

checks.name: all_classes_exactly_17_bytes
checks.evidence: Classes retain different semantic roles and aliased fields do not allocate new values. Common retained-history capacity can be chosen consistently for all classes; the contract explicitly calls it a bounded availability policy and claims zero entropy requirement. The historical positive_int maximum is a legitimate selected finite ceiling but is not an independently established mandatory ID cardinality.

checks.name: copy_json_reconstruction_and_wrapper
checks.evidence: Contract requires exact expected type, exact retained original object, private owner registry, retained upstream graph, immutable canonical bindings, HMAC and current eligibility; JSON/ID equality only correlates an authenticated exchange. No ID-only resolution path may grant authority.

checks.name: pid_fork_restart_and_reload
checks.evidence: PID is explicitly insufficient by itself. Fork invalidates inherited originals and lock/allocator use before issuance; restart may repeat text only in a disjoint new incarnation with new secrets/empty registry. Reload, registry replacement and secret rotation must retain namespace continuity or fail closed rather than restart counters.

checks.name: collision_terminal_and_tombstone
checks.evidence: Reservation/increment/collision check is linearizable; failure burns reservations. Reservation rejects preexisting reserved/live/terminal/tombstoned keys before claiming a fresh value. Registration may then publish only that issuer's own newly created reservation exactly once; foreign reservations and published/terminal/tombstoned values are rejected. This phase distinction avoids rejecting the issuer's legitimate reservation while preventing takeover or reuse. Histories survive operational object collection and terminal state; terminal evidence cannot reopen readiness.

checks.name: controller_attempt_deadline_and_nullable_scope
checks.evidence: Controller scalar is narrowed to original owner-object reference while source/protocol/generation bindings remain separate. Attempt is permanent materialize-to-compile relation with no refund/reopen. Deadline identifies an immutable monotonic deadline relation rather than a clock value. Borrower/handoff remain minimum-path null with nonnull encodings unestablished. Kernel/process/generation serialization and Candidate A selection remain out of scope.

checks.name: schema_and_authority_preservation
checks.evidence: The additive grammar fits unchanged generic nonempty <=256-byte string semantics. Challenge unpredictability, HMAC secrets, stable fingerprints, existing owner implementations, schema, transport selection and 8192-byte cap are preserved. Contract grants no effect or authority.

authority_anchor_resolution.actual_value: exact str, nonempty, <=256 UTF-8 bytes, no NUL; reference only to authenticated original relation, never restore authority from string

relevant_facts: registry retains original object/graph and permanent terminal tombstones
constant-time HMAC and retained canonical byte comparison

additional_anchor_resolution.actual_value: exact int in 1..9223372036854775807; bool rejected; no wrap/reuse

additional_anchor_resolution.evidence: Retains source/executable/protocol, original host/workspace relation, actual container, controller incarnation/generation, workspace generation, endpoints, bootstrap, limits and cleanup bindings.
Frozen message schema id definition is type=str, min_utf8_bytes=1, max_utf8_bytes=256 and NUL_allowed=false; additive 17-byte ASCII grammar fits it.

resolved_clarifications.previous_text: exact built-in expected type, rejecting wrappers and subclasses
resolved_clarifications.reason: Owner/relation objects are expected custom types. Built-in scalar type checks and exact owner-class checks are both required, so the current wording could be misread as allowing only built-in owner object types.
resolved_clarifications.resolution: Final contract says exact expected owner/relation object type, and exact built-in scalar types; reject wrappers and subclasses.

resolved_clarifications.reason: Historical positive_int constrains existing numeric sequence values, while historical ID schema permits generic strings. The chosen 63-bit ID allocation ceiling is defensible as a new bounded availability policy; it is not semantically required by that historical positive_int bound.
resolved_clarifications.resolution: Final capacity rationale explicitly chooses 63 bits as this phase's bounded availability policy, distinguishes historical sequence limits from generic ID strings, and accepts that 32-bit handles can also be security-correct with exhaustion.

allocation_coordination_separation: Final generation_semantics.allocation_is_not_coordination explicitly limits the reservation ledger to name uniqueness; it does not bridge owner stores, hold existing private locks, authenticate admissions, spend facets or establish effect transactions. This preserves the pure identity-contract scope.

final_collision_wording_review.evidence: Independently reread the amended reservation versus registration predicates. A fresh issuer reservation is not rejected merely because it exists at publication; the publication exception is limited to its creator, its newly reserved key and one publication. Failure/cancellation remains burned. No other namespace, authority, replay, lifetime or encoding rule changes.

scope_limit: This is contract coherence/security review, not implementation validation, a transport design, full budget proof, owner issuance test or claim that operational readiness exists.
